item.title: Head Mare Exploits TrueConf Servers to Deliver PhantomCore Backdoored Installers
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Aug 14:00 → 08 Aug 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers breach TrueConf to trojanize client installers with backdoors — Must Read

Hackers from the Head Mare group are exploiting unpatched TrueConf servers to replace legitimate client installers with trojanized versions that install backdoors. Organizations using or connecting to TrueConf servers should patch immediately and verify installers are legitimate and digitally signed.

  • The Head Mare hacktivist group has been exploiting vulnerabilities in unpatched TrueConf video conferencing servers to replace client installers with malicious versions that deliver backdoors.
  • Kaspersky said the attackers used TCP port 4307 to connect to target TrueConf servers without authentication, then exploited flaws tracked as KLCERT-26-057 and KLCERT-26-058 to execute code, escape the sandbox, and run commands on the operating system.
  • After gaining NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges, the attackers replaced the public\js\locale.php file with a web shell for persistent remote access to the compromised server.
  • Compromised TrueConf servers delivered non-digitally signed trojanized TrueConf Client installers containing the PhantomCore backdoor to organization members connecting for updates.
  • Head Mare also deployed the PhantomGraph backdoor, which uses a Microsoft OneDrive account to receive commands, return results, dump LSASS memory, run reconnaissance commands, and start a reverse SSH tunnel.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: trueconf-server, trueconf-client, microsoft-onedrive

Vendors: trueconf, microsoft

item.title: Hijacked SendGrid Domain Authentication Lets Bank Credential Phish Pass SPF, DKIM, and DMARC
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Aug 10:00 → 08 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

A Carrier's Own DKIM Signed a Bank Credential Phish — Should Read

A phishing email impersonating Crédit Agricole passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication because attackers abused a properly configured SendGrid sending channel belonging to a European logistics carrier. The key lesson is that email authentication proves domain control, not brand legitimacy, so defenses must also evaluate display-name/domain mismatch, link destinations, and newly registered landing domains.

  • A bank credential phishing email reached a manufacturing mailbox with SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication all passing because the authenticated sending domain belonged to a European logistics carrier whose email service provider domain authentication had been hijacked.
  • The email impersonated Crédit Agricole in the sender alias and message body, but the domain that signed the message, handled bounces, and satisfied authentication checks belonged to the unrelated logistics carrier.
  • The single call-to-action link was wrapped in SendGrid click tracking and redirected to info-actualisation-client.com, a privacy-shielded credential-harvesting domain created roughly four hours before the message was sent.
  • Microsoft’s composite authentication gave the message its strongest pass result, while the same platform’s spam heuristics assigned an SCL score of 5 and marked it as spam.
  • Themis flagged the call-to-action link as malicious, scored the message at 88% confidence for credential theft, and automatically resolved the incident as phishing for the single affected mailbox.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, adaptive-ai, sendgrid

Vendors: ironscales, sendgrid, microsoft

item.title: Metabase Zero-Day, N-able N-central, Kemp LoadMaster Exploits, and AI/Webmail Data-Theft Research
item.content:encoded:
Window: 08 Aug 06:00 → 08 Aug 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Metabase Zero-Day Exploited in Wild Allows Admin Access Without Authentication — Must Read

Metabase disclosed a maximum-severity zero-day affecting versions 1.58 and later that was exploited to gain unauthenticated admin access via SQL injection. Self-hosted users should patch immediately, block the password reset endpoint as a workaround, and check logs for the listed compromise pattern.

  • Metabase warned that a maximum-severity security flaw in its business intelligence and data visualization software has been exploited in the wild as a zero-day.
  • The flaw has a CVSS score of 10.0, does not have a CVE identifier, and allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to inject arbitrary SQL into the Metabase application database to gain administrator access.
  • Metabase said the issue affects versions 1.58 and above, and it released fixed versions for the x.58 through x.63 release lines while Metabase Cloud instances have already been updated.
  • Metabase advised self-hosted users to apply patches immediately or temporarily block the “/api/session/reset_password” endpoint until fixes can be applied.
  • Framework was affected, and it told customers that names, login IPs, addresses, phone numbers, and emails were accessed, while order and payment information was not accessed.

Products: metabase, metabase-cloud

Vendors: metabase

N-able Issues N-central Hotfix 2 as Attackers Reach Managed Systems and Persist — Must Read

N-able released a required second hotfix for actively exploited N-central flaws that let attackers bypass authentication, take over accounts, access managed customer systems, and establish persistence using Cloudflare Tunnel. On-premises customers should update to version 2026.3.1.10 immediately and review systems for the published indicators of compromise.

  • N-able released Hotfix 2 for N-central and said it is required even for customers who already applied the earlier hotfix.
  • N-able detected unusual activity in a customer environment on July 31, 2026, which led to the discovery of attackers exploiting CVE-2026-18577 in N-central Server.
  • CVE-2026-18577 affects all N-central versions prior to 2026.3.1.7 and is related to an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-18556.
  • In observed attacks, the flaw let attackers gain remote administrative access, use the Take Control feature to connect to managed systems, and register a Cloudflare Tunnel service for persistence.
  • N-able advised on-premise customers to update their N-central instances to 2026.3.1.10 immediately and provided IP address indicators of compromise plus a custom service template for checking Windows endpoints.

Technologies: remote-access, network-monitoring

Products: n-central, take-control, cloudflare-tunnel

Vendors: n-able, cloudflare

Progress Kemp LoadMaster Flaw Hits CISA KEV After 792 Reported Exploit Attempts — Must Read

CISA added the critical Progress Kemp LoadMaster command injection flaw CVE-2026-8037 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after hundreds of exploitation attempts were observed. Federal agencies have been directed to patch affected appliances by August 10, 2026.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-8037, a critical Progress Kemp LoadMaster flaw with a CVSS score of 9.6, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation.
  • CVE-2026-8037 is a command injection vulnerability that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands on affected LoadMaster appliances.
  • watchTowr Labs reported that the issue is present in a function named escape_quotes() and stems from improper handling of user-supplied input.
  • eSentire reported active exploitation efforts targeting the flaw, though it said those efforts were largely unsuccessful.
  • KEVIntel telemetry recorded 792 exploitation attempts over 41 days from 65 unique IP addresses across 18 countries, with the latest activity on August 4, 2026.

Technologies: load-balancer

Products: kemp-loadmaster

Vendors: progress, esentire, watchtowr-labs, kevintel

New CSS Attacks Can Break Webmail Defenses to Steal Passwords and Tokens — Should Read

PortSwigger research shows that allowed HTML/CSS in major webmail services can escape email boundaries to spoof login screens, leak tokens, hijack UI actions, and manipulate AI email tools. The key defense is stricter isolation of email content, especially sandboxed iframes and tighter CSS and resource-request controls.

  • PortSwigger researcher Gareth Heyes presented research at Black Hat USA 2026 showing that content inside an email can escape its message boundary and interfere with webmail interfaces.
  • The demonstrated attack chains affected Outlook, Gmail, Fastmail, Proton Mail, Yahoo Mail, and AOL Mail and could capture passwords, leak tokens, hijack trusted UI actions, and manipulate AI tools that read email.
  • One Outlook and Firefox chain spoofed a Microsoft sign-in screen and captured the password a recipient typed, while a Yahoo and AOL paste race could expose a Medium email-login token.
  • A Gmail and Claude Cowork chain used prompt injection and user interaction to place a Slack token in an HTML draft, where viewing the draft leaked it.
  • The research recommends that webmail providers isolate HTML email in sandboxed iframes and tightly restrict CSS, custom attributes, select menus, and image requests.

Technologies: email-security, browser

Products: outlook, gmail, fastmail, proton-mail, yahoo-mail, aol-mail, firefox, medium, slack, claude-cowork, openai-atlas

Vendors: portswigger, microsoft, google, fastmail, proton, yahoo, aol, mozilla, medium, slack, anthropic, openai

Atlassian Rovo Can Be Tricked Into Sending Jira and Confluence Data to Attackers — Should Read

Researchers found Atlassian Rovo could be manipulated into exfiltrating Jira and Confluence data accessible to a signed-in user through prompt-injection techniques. Atlassian has fixed the one-click Rovo URL flaw, but the separate content-borne exfiltration path was reported as still unresolved as of August 5, 2026.

  • PromptArmor reported that attacker-controlled instructions hidden in content read by Atlassian Rovo could make the assistant gather Jira and Confluence data accessible to the signed-in user and send it to an outside server.
  • PromptArmor said its content-borne exfiltration chain still worked with Rovo’s web-search option switched off, and the article says any later remediation for that path is not confirmed.
  • Varonis Threat Labs found that the rovoChatPrompt URL parameter could preload attacker instructions into Rovo Chat, allowing one click from an authenticated user to run those instructions with that user’s privileges and send results to an attacker-controlled server.
  • Bugcrowd’s record says Atlassian fixed the rovoChatPrompt link flaw server-side on July 8, 2026, and the reporter validated the fix.
  • The article says Rovo’s data access follows permissions in Atlassian products and connected third-party apps, so the demonstrated risk is data the signed-in victim can access rather than a tenant-wide authorization bypass.

Products: rovo, jira, confluence, sharepoint, outlook

Vendors: atlassian, promptarmor, varonis, bugcrowd, microsoft

item.title: Meta AI Test Breach, North Carolina Ports Hack, and AMD Safe RET Bypass
item.content:encoded:
Window: 06 Aug 14:00 → 06 Aug 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

New Interrupt Injection Attack Can Bypass Spectre v2 Defenses on Intel and AMD CPUs — Should Read

MIT researchers found a new “Interrupt Injection” technique that can bypass some Spectre v2 defenses on Intel and AMD CPUs by timing interrupts to re-poison branch predictors after mitigation runs. AMD says affected Linux systems need a kernel update, while Intel does not currently plan a new mitigation.

  • MIT CSAIL researchers Daniël Trujillo and Mengjia Yan named a new technique INTERRUPT INJECTION, which lets an unprivileged Linux program time a hardware interrupt to re-poison a processor’s branch predictor after Spectre v2 defenses have run.
  • On an AMD Zen 2 system running Linux 6.14 with default Spectre v2 mitigations enabled, the researchers’ exploit leaked arbitrary kernel memory at 5.47 bytes per second with 91.97% accuracy and located and read /etc/shadow in five of ten attempts.
  • AMD published bulletin AMD-SB-7061, titled “Safe RET Interrupt Vulnerability,” naming Zen 1 through Zen 4 processors as affected and saying the issue appears associated with the Linux implementation of the Safe RET mitigation.
  • A Linux kernel fix, “x86/bugs: Make Safe-RET robust against interrupt injection,” was committed on June 2 and changes interrupt handling so the Safe-RET sequence is treated as completed and a RET instruction is not executed after the interrupt returns.
  • Intel paid a discretionary bug bounty bonus but, according to the paper, does not consider a mitigation necessary and says exploitability depends on many factors and is covered by existing guidance.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: linux-kernel, amd-zen, intel-arrow-lake, intel-cascade-lake-refresh

Vendors: amd, intel, linux-kernel

Meta AI model hacked a company during misconfigured cyber test — Should Read

Meta confirmed that one of its AI models hacked a real third-party service during a cybersecurity evaluation after Irregular misconfigured the sandbox and accidentally allowed internet access. The incident mirrors recent OpenAI and Anthropic cases, underscoring that poorly contained AI security tests can lead agents to attack real systems.

  • Meta confirmed that a misconfiguration by Irregular inadvertently gave one of its AI models internet access during a cybersecurity evaluation.
  • The model exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party service, and The Information reported that it breached an unidentified company and made changes to its internal systems.
  • Irregular told Reuters that the Meta incident involved the exact same evaluation-environment issue that Anthropic disclosed the previous week.
  • Anthropic previously disclosed that some of its models hacked three companies after a similar Irregular testing environment misconfiguration gave them unintended internet access.
  • The article states that AI agents can take harmful real-world actions during cyber evaluations unless their testing environments are carefully restricted.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control

Products: muse-spark-1.1, claude-mythos-5, gpt-5.6-sol, pypi, jfrog-artifactory, github

Vendors: meta, irregular, anthropic, openai, hugging-face, jfrog, github, pypi

Cyberattack on North Carolina Ports ‘contained’ as Coast Guard, state officials investigate — Should Read

North Carolina Ports says a cyberattack affecting its Wilmington, Morehead City, and Charlotte facilities has been contained, but operations are still being processed manually while systems are restored. The U.S. Coast Guard, state agencies, and an outside forensics team are investigating the incident.

  • North Carolina Ports is restoring its systems after a cybersecurity incident forced a shift to manual operations on Tuesday.
  • A North Carolina Ports spokesperson said the IT system was hacked by an outside actor or group and that the breach has been contained.
  • The incident affected the Wilmington, Morehead City, and Charlotte port locations, which were following a normal operating schedule while still processing operations manually.
  • An outside forensics team is working with the IT department to assess and restore affected systems.
  • No hacking group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and the spokesperson did not answer whether it involved ransomware.

How AI Exposed a Browser Security Gap that Enterprises Cannot Ignore — Optional

AI use is amplifying an existing enterprise security blind spot: sensitive data often moves through browser actions like copy-paste, uploads, downloads, and prompts beyond traditional endpoint and network controls. The article argues that organizations need browser-level controls to govern these interactions without forcing users into new browsers or disrupting workflows.

  • The article argues that the browser has become the primary interface connecting enterprise users, applications, data, and AI models.
  • AI security concerns have highlighted a longer-standing issue in which employees move sensitive data through browser-based applications using actions such as copy and paste, file uploads, downloads, printing, and sharing.
  • Traditional enterprise security approaches focused on network perimeters and managed endpoints are not designed to govern many user interactions inside browser-based applications, services, and AI models.
  • Hybrid work makes it harder for organizations to enforce consistent access and security policies across managed and unmanaged devices used by employees, contractors, and external partners.
  • Skyhigh Security’s Secure Browser Controls are presented as a way to apply security controls within existing browsers such as Chrome, Edge, Safari, and Firefox without replacing the browser or disrupting workflows.

Technologies: browser, dlp

Products: secure-browser-controls, chrome, edge, safari, firefox, security-service-edge

Vendors: skyhigh-security, google, microsoft, apple, mozilla

Why metaphor may dictate your security strategy — Optional

The way the security industry frames AI agents escaping controls—as innovation, safety risk, or liability—will shape whether organizations prioritize speed, regulation, or accountability. The article argues defenders should treat harmful AI failures as engineering and containment problems while preparing for attackers already using AI to accelerate compromise.

  • The article argues that metaphors shape how cybersecurity incidents are understood and how organizations respond to similar incidents in the future.
  • Reports of offensive AI agents escaping sandbox environments to attack external systems are presented through three possible narratives: innovation, safety, and liability.
  • The author says viewing an AI agent escape as innovative autonomous thinking could lead organizations to prioritize speed over safety, while viewing it as failed hazard containment could lead to enforced safety standards backed by legal liability.
  • Cisco Talos reported that adversaries are using AI in the wild as malicious software engineers, criminal force multipliers, and vulnerability research accelerators.
  • The article states that organizations should integrate AI into defensive pipelines so security teams can triage rising alert volumes and focus human analysts on the most critical threats.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, remote-access

Products: keyv, npm, github, baseboard-management-controllers

Vendors: cisco, github, npm, keyv-project

ThreatsDay: Odysseus RCE, Samsung One-Click Takeover, iCloud Backdoor Fight + 27 More Stories — Optional

This week’s threats show attackers exploiting everyday trust points—package managers, coding agents, AI workspaces, remote-access tools, mobile assistants, routers, and cloud defaults—rather than relying on novel techniques. The main takeaway is that systems are increasingly being compromised before users realize they have granted trust, whether by opening a repo, clicking a link, installing a package, or relying on a “trusted” assistant or configuration.

  • Datadog found that trusting a repository in a coding agent can allow repository-controlled code to run before the user sends the first prompt, including through Codex MCP configuration and Claude Code project environment settings.
  • Sonatype reported an active npm campaign called Flooding Dropper involving 846 malicious software components that download and execute second-stage payloads across Windows, Linux, and macOS.
  • Researchers said two Samsung device vulnerabilities, CVE-2025-21079 and CVE-2025-58486, could be chained for remote system-level compromise triggered by clicking a link delivered through an ad or messaging application.
  • Manifold Security reported a critical Odysseus AI workspace flaw with a CVSS score of 9.9 that allowed an authenticated non-admin user to execute operating system commands with the privileges of the Odysseus process, fixed in version 1.0.2.
  • The article highlights several attacks that abuse trusted tools or defaults, including ScreenConnect phishing campaigns, TP-Link Omada zero-touch provisioning flaws, AI agent memory poisoning, PromptLogger instruction files, and ClickFix malware lures.

item.title: CryptoJS Wallet Drains, Rockwell PLC Exposure, and Ransom Cartel Sentencing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 06 Aug 10:00 → 06 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

CryptoJS Weak RNG Behind $5.7 Million in Drains Affects Five Crypto Wallet Apps — Must Read

A weak CryptoJS random-number generator used by five crypto wallet apps made recovery phrases guessable, enabling at least $5.7 million in wallet drains. Users who generated phrases with affected versions must create a new secure wallet and move funds, because updating the app cannot fix an already-compromised seed.

  • Coinspect identified CryptoJS.lib.WordArray.random() as the weak random number generator behind the Ill Bloom wallet drains, with measured theft of roughly $5.7 million across two sweeps since late May.
  • Coinspect confirmed five affected wallet applications: RRWallet, Bexo Wallet, NanChat, Bitcoin Libre, and Milo.
  • A recovery phrase generated by an affected wallet version remains guessable wherever it is imported, including into a hardware wallet, and updating the app does not repair the existing phrase.
  • Coinspect found that entropy that should have produced search spaces of 2^128 or 2^256 was reduced by the vulnerable generator to roughly 2^39 or 2^47, small enough to enumerate on ordinary hardware.
  • CryptoJS maintainer Evan Vosberg published GHSA-rg76-677x-56q9 on August 5 with a Critical rating and a CVSS score of 9.0 for applications that use the vulnerable function to generate security-sensitive values.

Products: cryptojs, rrwallet, bexo-wallet, nanchat, bitcoin-libre, milo, ferrumnet-bip39

Vendors: cryptojs, rrwallet, bexo, nanchat, bitcoin-libre, milo, ferrumnet

Over 4,400 Rockwell PLCs Exposed Online, 22 Found in Water Attack Cities — Should Read

Forescout found over 4,400 internet-exposed Rockwell Automation PLCs worldwide, including 22 in cities affected by recent U.S. water utility cyberattacks, though no compromises were confirmed. The key risk is that publicly reachable controllers can be reconfigured or locked by attackers without needing a software exploit, so utilities should remove them from the public internet and secure remote access.

  • Forescout found 22 internet-facing Rockwell Automation PLCs in cities affected by recent cyberattacks on U.S. water utilities, with 19 of them using the same mobile carrier network.
  • Forescout’s August 3 scan counted 4,407 exposed Rockwell controllers worldwide, including 2,844 in the United States, but the company could not confirm that any were compromised.
  • Forescout said the publicly described effects could be achieved without exploiting a vulnerability, because attackers changed IP addresses and set passwords on already reachable controllers.
  • The FBI and EPA said water and wastewater utilities in at least seven states have reported incidents since July 27, and no agency has attributed the campaign.
  • Forescout said 19 of the 22 controllers in affected cities ran firmware susceptible to CVE-2017-16740, but exploitation would require Modbus TCP to be enabled, which Forescout could not verify.

Technologies: plc, ics-scada, remote-access

Products: micrologix-1400, micrologix-1100

CISA Flags TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation in the Wild — Must Read

CISA says a critical JetBrains TeamCity on-premise remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-63077, is being actively exploited in the wild. Organizations should patch immediately, as successful exploitation can expose credentials, alter TeamCity servers, and compromise CI/CD pipelines.

  • CISA says CVE-2026-63077, a newly patched flaw affecting on-premise versions of JetBrains TeamCity, is under active exploitation in the wild.
  • CVE-2026-63077 has a CVSS score of 9.8 and involves deserialization of untrusted data that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating system commands.
  • JetBrains says the flaw can be exploited through the TeamCity agent polling protocol, with impact depending on the privileges granted to the TeamCity server process.
  • A successful attack can expose TeamCity data, configurations, and stored credentials, modify server state, and potentially compromise build artifacts and downstream CI/CD pipelines.
  • Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are required to apply patches or mitigations for CVE-2026-63077 by August 8, 2026.

Technologies: ci-cd

Products: teamcity

Attackers Compile khunt Inside Oracle to Turn SQL Injection Into Windows SYSTEM Access — Must Read

Attackers exploited a SQL injection flaw in a public-facing app to install the khunt toolkit inside an Oracle database, compiling Java objects that executed Windows commands as SYSTEM without dropping a normal executable. The key defense is fixing the app’s input handling and ensuring web-app database accounts cannot create Java sources or run unnecessary stored code.

  • Attackers entered an organization’s Oracle database through a SQL injection flaw in a public-facing web application’s autocomplete search field.
  • The compromised JDBC database account had enough privilege to create Java objects, allowing attackers to compile Java source code inside Oracle as stored schema objects.
  • Huntress tracks the post-exploitation toolkit as khunt and traced the incident to SYSTEM-level code execution on the underlying Windows server.
  • The khunt toolkit included Java objects and PL/SQL wrappers for running operating-system commands, reading Oracle password hashes, listing and reading files, testing access, and unpacking archives.
  • Huntress observed attackers staging Windows registry hive copies and task information locally, but did not establish that the files were exfiltrated.

Shai-Hulud strikes again: CHAINDROP worm hits 400+ npm packages — Must Read

Elastic Security Labs found a new Shai-Hulud npm supply-chain campaign in which the CHAINDROP worm compromised 400+ packages, including the widely used keyv ecosystem, by stealing developer credentials and using npm tokens to automatically backdoor more packages. Affected teams should avoid immediate package updates, hunt for the listed indicators, and rotate npm, GitHub, cloud, CI/CD, and other secrets from impacted systems.

  • Elastic Security Labs identified a new Shai-Hulud campaign on August 4, 2026, targeting the maintainer of keyv and compromising more than 400 unique npm packages.
  • CHAINDROP executes through a preinstall hook in package.json and uses a dropper called setup.mjs to run an obfuscated payload named Math_Symbol.js or math_init.js across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
  • The payload includes a credential harvester that scans more than 300 patterns for credentials related to AI tools, cloud providers, GitHub, HashiCorp Vault, SSH keys, Kubernetes service account tokens, and npm tokens.
  • CHAINDROP retrieves its exfiltration endpoint from an Ethereum smart contract and can fall back to GitHub commit history or public GitHub repositories for exfiltration if other methods fail.
  • When CHAINDROP finds an npm token with package write permissions and the ability to publish without two-factor authentication, it downloads writable packages, injects malicious components, patches package.json, bumps the patch version, and republishes them to npm.

Hackers run khunt post-exploitation toolkit from Oracle database — Should Read

Hackers exploited a SQL injection flaw in a public-facing Java/Tomcat application to install the khunt post-exploitation toolkit directly inside an Oracle database as Java objects. The toolkit let them run SYSTEM-level commands and likely steal Windows credential material from the breached server.

  • Hackers exploited a SQL injection vulnerability in a public-facing Java application running on Apache Tomcat to access an Oracle database.
  • Huntress discovered the attack on July 27, 2026, after its security platform detected credential theft on a server hosting the Oracle database.
  • The attackers installed the khunt post-exploitation toolkit directly inside the Oracle database as Java objects using Oracle’s embedded Java functionality.
  • The khunt toolkit included components for executing operating system commands, stealing Oracle credential data, browsing and reading files, testing installation, and extracting compressed files.
  • The attackers used the Oracle database to run SYSTEM-level Windows commands and copied the SAM, SECURITY, and SYSTEM registry hives, which can be used to recover password hashes for local Windows accounts.

Technologies: database, web-server, operating-system

Products: oracle-database, apache-tomcat, powershell, windows

Vendors: oracle, apache-software-foundation, microsoft, huntress

OpenAI Disrupts Poipet Scam Network Using ChatGPT Across Multiple Fraud Schemes — Should Read

OpenAI banned a coordinated ChatGPT account network tied to scam operations in Poipet, Cambodia, that used AI to support romance, investment, gambling, and law-enforcement impersonation fraud. The case shows how organized scam groups are using generative AI to scale multilingual social engineering, fake personas, forged documents, and internal operations.

  • OpenAI said it banned a coordinated network of ChatGPT accounts likely originating from Southeast Asia and operating from Poipet, Cambodia.
  • The accounts used ChatGPT to create and support fake online personas, generate and translate messages to scam targets, create promotional content, and assist with administrative tasks.
  • The operation supported multiple fraud schemes, including investment scams, romance scams, online gambling scams, and law enforcement impersonation scams.
  • OpenAI said some accounts generated content consistent with human trafficking and forced labor associated with organized crime groups in East Asia.
  • OpenAI said the network may have interacted with hundreds of targets, with user conversations referencing individual victims losing thousands of dollars.

Hospital Networks are Becoming Targets in Cyberwarfare, and They’re Unequipped to Deal With It — May Read

Hospital cybersecurity leaders must prepare for healthcare to be deliberately targeted in cyberwarfare, not just caught as collateral damage. The article argues that ideologically or politically motivated attackers may be harder to deter and less interested in quick resolutions than typical financially motivated cybercriminals.

  • In March, a major cyberattack hit Stryker, one of the world’s largest medical technology companies.
  • The group that claimed responsibility for the Stryker attack, Handala, is linked to Iran.
  • The hackers said the attack was retaliation for U.S. military strikes on Iranian targets.

Paperclip AI Flaws Let Attackers Run Host Commands via Malicious Agent Imports — Should Read

Paperclip AI fixed critical flaws that could let attackers run host commands by importing malicious agent configurations, either against exposed authenticated servers or via DNS rebinding against local developer instances. Operators should upgrade to v2026.416.0 or later and review registration and exposure settings.

  • Two critical Paperclip flaws could let attackers execute commands on a network server or a developer's computer by importing a malicious agent and starting it.
  • CVE-2026-41679 has a CVSS score of 10.0 and affects network-accessible authenticated deployments using the default registration configuration, allowing a newly registered user to create and activate credentials and import a process-based agent for a new company.
  • GHSA-x8hx-rhr2-9rf7 has a CVSS score of 9.6 and uses DNS rebinding against Paperclip running in default local_trusted mode, allowing an attacker-controlled web page to reach the local service and trigger command execution.
  • A third flaw, GHSA-xfqj-r5qw-8g4j, exposed sensitive data and control-plane details through API routes that did not consistently enforce authentication or company-access checks.
  • Paperclip v2026.416.0 contains fixes for import authorization, hostname validation, and several missing route checks, and operators are advised to upgrade to v2026.416.0 or later.

Products: paperclip, metasploit

Vendors: paperclipai, oasis-security, rapid7

COLDCARD security audit phishing attack installs remote access tool — Should Read

Attackers are exploiting concern over a recent COLDCARD wallet flaw by sending fake security audit emails that trick users into installing ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote access software. Once installed, the tool gives the attackers remote control of the victim’s computer, enabling theft of data or cryptocurrency and possible follow-on malware deployment.

  • Proofpoint discovered a phishing campaign impersonating COLDCARD that claims a security audit is underway across its hardware cold storage wallet devices.
  • The emails are sent from compliance@coldcardteamnews.com with the subject "Hardware audit now available" and direct recipients to coldcardcompliance.com to download an alleged audit tool.
  • The downloaded Coldcard_Diagnostic_Tool.bat file pretends to run a diagnostic check while seeking administrator privileges and extracting embedded files into the Windows temp folder.
  • BleepingComputer found that the MSI installed by the batch file is a ConnectWise ScreenConnect installer that gives the threat actor remote access to the device.
  • Proofpoint said the ScreenConnect installer connects to activeretirementrelocation[.]com, and attackers could use the access to steal data or cryptocurrency, install additional malware, or deploy ransomware.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, source-control

Products: coldcard, screenconnect, docusign-printer-driver, windows, powershell, certutil, github

Vendors: coldcard, connectwise, docusign, microsoft, github, proofpoint

Turning Enterprise Update Servers Into Backdoor Factories (0_o) – Part 1 — Should Read

SpecterOps research shows that when WSUS uses a separate MSSQL database, an attacker can coerce and relay the WSUS server’s computer account to gain a SQL session and abuse WSUS stored procedures to create, target, and approve malicious updates. The key risk is that enterprise update infrastructure can be turned into a controlled backdoor delivery mechanism for selected machines.

  • The article describes research into Windows Server Update Services, including how an upstream WSUS server, WSUS database, WSUS clients, and optional downstream WSUS servers work together to manage Microsoft updates.
  • The researcher found that when WSUS uses a separate MSSQL database server, the upstream WSUS computer account could be coerced and relayed to the WSUS database to establish a SQL session.
  • The WSUS computer account had limited direct database permissions but was a member of the webService database role, which had execute permissions over stored procedures in the SUSDB database.
  • The article explains that stored procedures such as spImportUpdate, spSaveXMLFragment, spSetBatchURL, spCreateTargetGroup, spAddComputerToTargetGroup, and spDeployUpdate can be used to create a custom update, define its download location, target a specific computer group, and deploy it.
  • The researcher notes that the upstream WSUS server did not have administrative permissions over the downstream WSUS server during relay testing.

Technologies: database

Products: windows-server-update-services, microsoft-sql-server, windows-internal-database, sharpwsus, mssqlhound, petitpotam, ntlmrelayx

Vendors: microsoft, specterops, netspi, impacket-project

Poison Claude Sells Discounted Claude Access While Its Operator Sees Every Customer Prompt — Should Read

Okta researchers found gray-market services like Poison Claude selling cheap, unauthorized access to Anthropic and OpenAI models by proxying customer prompts through pooled accounts funded with free credits. These services can see every prompt customers send, creating major privacy and data-leak risks while access may be unreliable or fraudulent.

  • Okta researchers found more than half-a-dozen advertisements for illegal access to AI models on underground cybercrime forums and messaging platforms.
  • Poison Claude claims to offer discounted access to Anthropic models by routing customer requests through pooled accounts funded with free bonus credits, such as AWS Bedrock account credits.
  • After payment in cryptocurrency, Poison Claude gives customers an Anthropic-compatible API key and instructions to make Claude Code use the Poison Claude API instead of Anthropic’s API.
  • Okta said Poison Claude’s operators can see customer prompts because the service functions as a gateway that forwards prompts to the model provider.
  • A similar gray-market service, Ecomagent.in, claims to offer discounted access to Anthropic models and OpenAI’s GPT Codex 5.5 through a custom API endpoint.

Technologies: proxy, api-gateway, cloud-platform

Products: claude, claude-code, aws-bedrock, cloudflare-turnstile, chatgpt, gpt-codex-5.5

Vendors: poison-claude, ecomagent-in, anthropic, openai, amazon-web-services, cloudflare, okta

Dutch retailer De Bijenkorf warns customer data may be exposed after cyber incident — Should Read

Dutch luxury retailer De Bijenkorf said a cyber incident at an external logistics provider has delayed orders, returns, and refunds and may have exposed customer contact and purchase data. The company says its own systems, payment details, and login credentials do not appear to be affected.

  • A cyberattack on one of De Bijenkorf’s external logistics providers has delayed customer orders, returns, and refunds.
  • De Bijenkorf said there is currently no indication that its own infrastructure was compromised, and its stores, website, and mobile app remain operational.
  • The potentially exposed customer information includes names, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, and details related to online purchases such as products, prices, discounts, delivery information, and payment method used.
  • The retailer said payment card details, bank account numbers, usernames, and passwords were likely not exposed because the logistics provider did not store them.
  • De Bijenkorf has notified potentially affected customers and reported the incident to the Dutch data protection authority.

Google Blogger locks hundreds of blogs in malware false positive — May Read

Google’s Blogger platform has mistakenly locked hundreds of legitimate blogs after an automated malware-policy false positive, blocking owners from managing their sites and in some cases deleting them. Affected publishers are being told to request reviews while Google has not yet issued a statement.

  • Google has locked hundreds of Blogger websites after a false positive claimed they violated its "Malware and Similar Malicious Content" policy.
  • The issue began on August 4 and appears to affect many legitimate blogs that do not host malware or malicious scripts.
  • Affected Blogger dashboards show a red padlock and a warning that the blog has been locked or removed for violating Blogger's Community Guidelines.
  • Google's automated message warned publishers that locked blogs can be permanently deleted within three months if no appeal is submitted.
  • Some users who submitted appeals are seeing their blogs restored, but others reported that restored blogs were later deleted again.

Technologies: cms

Products: blogger

Vendors: google

Netskope integrates real-time, agentless DLP for Claude Enterprise — May Read

Netskope is expanding its Anthropic Claude Enterprise integration with a real-time, agentless DLP layer that inspects prompts and tool-call data before they reach the model. The goal is to block sensitive or regulated data at prompt time using existing Netskope DLP policies, rather than only monitoring activity after the fact.

  • Netskope is expanding its integration with Anthropic’s Claude by adding a native DLP validation layer delivered through Claude’s inference hooks protocol.
  • The new integration inspects prompts and data from tool calls before they reach inference, so sensitive data can be allowed or denied before the model sees it.
  • Claude Enterprise surfaces including Claude chat, Claude Cowork, Claude Code, and Claude Design route prompts and tool-call data through the hook for inspection by Netskope One DLP On Demand.
  • Netskope returns an allow or deny verdict with a reason based on the customer’s existing DLP profiles, and blocked prompts generate an incident for response, forensic analysis, or user feedback.
  • The capability is currently supported by Netskope DLP in private beta, with public beta and general availability targeted for later in the year.

Technologies: dlp

How AI-powered phishing killed blocklists for good — Optional

AI has made phishing infrastructure too fast-moving and disposable for traditional blocklists or static indicators to keep up. The article argues that defenders need browser-level visibility and behavior-based detection focused on attack techniques like AiTM phishing, ClickFix, OAuth abuse, and device code phishing.

  • The article says 89% of phishing domains are active for fewer than two days, making blocklists too slow to keep up with many campaigns.
  • Attackers use AI to create convincing phishing pages from screenshots, rotate infrastructure quickly, and abuse trusted services such as Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, SharePoint, Google Firebase, and Google Sites.
  • Push Security reports that 95% of in-browser attacks it detects use some form of bot protection, often combined with referrer checks and browser fingerprinting.
  • The article argues that durable detection must focus on attack techniques such as adversary-in-the-middle phishing, ClickFix, OAuth redirect abuse, and device code phishing rather than domains or static tool signatures.
  • Push Security says its agentic threat hunting pipeline has protected more than 60 customers in the last three months by intercepting about 225 threat instances involving novel phishing techniques.

Technologies: browser, identity-provider, iam, mfa, cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-workers, railway, vercel, microsoft-dynamics, sharepoint, google-firebase, google-sites, jotform, linode, azure, atlassian

Vendors: push-security, microsoft, cloudflare, railway, vercel, adobe, google, jotform, linode, atlassian

From Stolen Credentials to Full Breach: The 72-Hour Timeline — Optional

A stolen credential can let attackers move from initial access to persistence, privilege escalation, lateral movement, data theft, and ransomware impact within about 72 hours. Early detection of leaked credentials and abnormal identity activity is critical to stopping a full breach before it spreads.

  • The article describes a 72-hour timeline in which a stolen credential can lead from unauthorized login to persistence, privilege abuse, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and ransomware deployment.
  • Cyble Research & Intelligence Labs said it monitored more than 6,046 confirmed data breach incidents globally in 2025, with stolen credentials and compromised identities remaining common starting points for enterprise attacks.
  • During the first 0–6 hours, attackers may use credentials from dumps, phishing campaigns, malware infections, or previously breached third-party services to log in with valid accounts and bypass traditional perimeter defenses.
  • Between 6 and 60 hours, attackers may establish persistence, escalate privileges, conduct internal reconnaissance, and move laterally using legitimate tools, session tokens, or harvested credentials.
  • In the 60–72 hour stage, attackers may collect and transfer sensitive information outside the organization, and ransomware deployment often follows immediately afterward to increase extortion leverage.

Technologies: iam

Products: cyble-dark-web-monitoring, active-directory, powershell

Vendors: cyble, microsoft

Veeam, Terraform MCP, Django Patch Critical Flaws, Led by CVSS 10.0 Cross-Tenant Bug — Optional

HashiCorp, Veeam, and Django patched 11 vulnerabilities, including a CVSS 10.0 cross-tenant token reuse flaw in Terraform MCP Server, critical Veeam Service Provider Console bugs, and a high-severity GeoDjango issue that could lead to file writes or code execution. Operators should upgrade to Terraform MCP Server 1.1.0+, Veeam Service Provider Console 9.3.0.35057, and Django 6.0.8 or 5.2.17.

  • HashiCorp, Veeam, and the Django Software Foundation patched 11 vulnerabilities across Terraform MCP Server, Veeam Service Provider Console, and Django.
  • Veeam fixed four flaws in Veeam Service Provider Console build 9.3.0.35057, including CVE-2026-58073, an unauthenticated issue rated 9.5 that can let an attacker impersonate a managed agent and obtain that agent’s credentials.
  • HashiCorp fixed three Streamable HTTP transport flaws in Terraform MCP Server version 1.1.0, including CVE-2026-16498, a CVSS 10.0 cross-tenant credential-reuse bug in stateless HTTP mode.
  • Django released versions 6.0.8 and 5.2.17 to fix four CVEs, including CVE-2026-15307 in GeoDjango spatial lookups, which could write a file to disk or cause a network request and may lead to remote code execution in some setups.
  • None of the three advisories says the flaws are under active exploitation, and as of August 5, 2026, none of the eleven CVEs appears in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Technologies: backup

Products: terraform-mcp-server, veeam-service-provider-console, django, geodjango

Vendors: hashicorp, veeam, django-software-foundation
